s.g: An aranga (burial scaffold traditionally used by Yakuts, Buryats, Tofalars, Evenks, Orochons and some other native nations of Siberia and the Russian Far East)
spring song, vesnianka (Eastern Slavic ritual song and dance)
spring draba, shadflower, nailwort, whitlowgrass (Draba verna)
to be recovered, to replaced, to repaid or recouped
ascent, rise (act of ascending; motion upwards)
to get used, to get accustomed (to), to feel at home (with), to take (to), to develop a liking (for), to begin to enjoy
to move out (to vacate one's place of residence)
madam, ma'am, Mrs., Miss (polite, formal term of address for a woman)
lady, mistress (the mistress of a household of servants or a manor)
mistress (term of address by a submissive partner to a dominant woman)
to stop leaking (due to swelling from moisture; of wooden vessels)
to appear (of tears in the eyes)
to turn up, to appear unexpectedly (somewhere)
requiescat (a prayer recited over the dying)
hydrogen peroxide, esp. about hair or their color whitened by using hydrogen peroxide
to go (in a conveyance or on horseback)
to go mad/insane, to lose one's mind
ellipsis of води́тельские права́ (vodítelʹskije pravá): driver's license
